whatTheyArgued: Gilbert (1912 BC Fisheries report, verified in text) argues from scale-age data that the Fraser sockeye run is mostly four-year-olds but includes three- and five-year fish, probing the four-year-cycle theory. In the same report he speculates that young may disperse in the sea and reassemble off the Strait of Fuca 'when approaching maturity leads them back toward their natal stream', i.e. a fan-like dispersal and reverse movement. He gives no curve, no timing function, no 'pull that grows as the fish nears home'. Modern homing science (Hasler & Scholz 1983) attributes freshwater homing mainly to olfactory imprinting on home-stream water.

scholarship.ref: Hasler & Scholz 1983, Olfactory Imprinting and Homing in Salmon (as reported in search results; pdf fetch blocked 403)
scholarship.supports: salmon imprint on home-stream odor as smolts and use it as adults; homing in fresh water is olfactory
scholarship.disputes: ocean-phase navigation is a separate, partly unresolved question; I could not read the page text
